targets.approach: Walk the Tahquitz north face trail, then go on toward Indian Buttress along faint paths that hug the creek. Once you are almost beneath Indian Buttress, cross the creek and climb the ravine to the foot of the Amphitheater itself, at the right-hand end of the First Terrace. The cirque as a whole is reached by way of the Strawberry Creek drainage. The route starts in a chimney and layback section that leads to a big pine tree.
targets.descent_text: From the top of the last pitch, hike down to the Devil's Slide trail, which returns to Humber Park.
targets.name: Crooked piton

targets.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. The route is on the right side of the left-hand of the two formations above Arctic Lakes and begins on orange, featured rock.
targets.descent_text: Travel west from the summit, then turn south and descend back to the lakes.
targets.name: Chillin The Most

targets.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. To find the start, look for the largest double-roof feature on the wall, then follow the single vertical crack at the left edge of those roofs down to the ground. The route starts in a flaky corner system there.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to the left from the top and follow the sandy slope back down.
targets.name: Cooler Than a Polar Bear's Toenails

targets.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. The route starts at a distinct orange corner, to the right of the West Arete route, and takes a direct line toward the western summit of the formation.
targets.descent_text: Descend by the gentle slopes along the west ridge.
targets.name: Polar Express

targets.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. This route is not on the main wall. It is on a smaller wall just above the lower camp below Arctic Lake Wall. Find the second large boulder to the right of a black streak; a clean crack splits the face above, with a stem-box chimney in the middle.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to the right from the top.
targets.name: Small Everything Blizzard

targets.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. The route starts just off the trail. The variation start begins up the bolted route immediately to its left, then cuts right to a stance below the anchor of Mine's Eye.
targets.name: Mine In The Sky

targets.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Never Mined starts at a wide crack just to the right of Mine Over Matter.
targets.name: Never Mined

targets.approach: From Road's End in Kings Canyon, hike east on the trail to the good camp just past Charlotte Creek. From camp, continue a short distance to a climbers' trail and follow the cairns up into a steep dry streambed. Near its top, bear left into the main gully that ends the right side of the whole wall. The route climbs the first few pitches of Ikigai before splitting off toward the golden headwall.
targets.name: The Ecstasy of Gold

targets.approach: Burnt Granola is the squarish cliff just north of where Highway 178 meets Chimney Peak Road. Park where Chimney Peak Road heads east under the cliff and walk a short way to the base. The route follows the center of the face to two obvious water cracks.
targets.name: Burnt Granola

targets.approach: Head up the John Muir Trail toward Cathedral Lakes. After the second set of switchbacks, when the tip of the wall first shows, keep walking until the trail crosses the creek and climbs another set of switchbacks, then leave the trail and walk cross-country straight at the wall; the going is open, with no thick brush. The route is a direct line toward the top of the wall, and the corner that dominates the fourth pitch is the feature to aim for.
targets.name: The Direct Line

targets.approach: The formation is visible from Tioga Road near the Porcupine Creek trailhead. There is no trail: park at a pullout on either side of the formation (the one just east works a little better) and find your own way across the ground to the rocks. Pleasant View Arete follows the southwest arete of the southern formation.
targets.name: Pleasant View Arete

targets.approach: From the Pine Creek trailhead, an old road and then a trail lead to Lower Pine Lake. Go beyond Upper Pine Lake, but turn left before reaching Honeymoon Lake and cross Pine Creek Pass and drop into French Canyon. Where the first big waterfall tumbles down on the right from Merriam Peak's flanks, you reach the wall. The route climbs beside the waterfall, up a right-facing dihedral that turns into an arete.
targets.name: Meet Your Shower
targets.parent: Humphreys Basin, Pine Creek & Granite Park

targets.approach: Take Gleason Ranch Road to the point beneath the rock and walk up from there; the other option is to come in from the east off Highway 178. The only route on the pyramid-shaped peak's north face begins in a fourth-class slot chimney.
targets.name: Bad Sneakers

targets.approach: Grouse Tor is the rounded summit east of the Grouse Ridge lookout; an easy walk from the parking area before the campground leads to the top, and a north-facing wall sits above Sanford Lake. Look for it at the rear of the big plateau high on the right side of the wall: after topping out Corn Silk, look right for a lone bleached pine in the talus field; the route is on the slab behind that tree. Another way to reach the plateau is to scramble down onto it from the face's west side.
targets.name: Wasted At IKEA

targets.approach: Cross Taboose Pass to the John Muir Trail, then go north on it to the crossing of the South Fork of the Kings River. Shortly past the crossing a use trail heads southwest toward Cartridge Pass. Follow its faint tread past some lakes and over the low point between Cirque Crest and Mt. Ruskin, then down past the lakes until the Hershey's Kiss face appears; there are good campsites along the lakes. Wonka's Way goes up the left portion of the main steep face, immediately right of the broken lower-angle gullies, and starts on low-angle slabs below a large left-facing corner.
targets.name: Wonka's Way

targets.approach: Starting in the Lakes Basin, cross the ridge and descend the gully; the wall towers on the gully's east side. Swish Dike climbs straight toward the face's high point, which lies left of center.
targets.name: Swish Dike

targets.approach: Park at the Lake George lot and take the Crystal Lake trail; at the Crystal Lake sign, turn left and descend to the lake. Walk around the lake, and a little farther on, a climbers trail branches left to the foot of the cliff. Highlands Wall is the first cliff reached, a northeast-facing wall visible from the parking lot. The route begins in the large chimney at the far left end of the wall, with the bolted crystal-dike route You Only Live Twice on its left and No Time To Die on its right.
targets.name: Northeast Buttress

targets.approach: Go high up the Hinterland Gully to the south side of its left flank; the climb starts in a left-facing corner, at the same start as Ridgeback.
targets.descent_text: From the bushy ledge at the top of the second pitch, head west along the ledge to trees under Ridgeback, then rappel off those trees into a loose gully.
targets.name: Breathing Space

targets.approach: The route is on the far left side of Hinterland Wall and begins in a left-facing dihedral.
targets.descent_text: The top anchor has rappel hangers that are not suitable for lowering, so rappel only. For a rappel of just the first pitch, use the anchor left of the trees.
targets.name: Aquarium

targets.approach: The route is on Hinterland Wall and shares its first-pitch dihedral start with the route Aquarium, at the far left side of the wall.
targets.name: Natural Mystic

targets.approach: Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. The route starts in a large notch in the middle of the boulder pile.
targets.name: Evelyn's Playground

targets.approach: Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. Look for a big chimney shaped like the letter A at the right end of the lower cliff; the route enters it from the bottom and follows the crack system above all the way to the summit.
targets.name: The "EH" Team

targets.approach: Follow the north talus approach to Tahquitz's north face and the North Gully descent, then continue much farther. The Indian Buttress formation lies just beyond the Hinterland cirque, deep in the cirque known as the Others.
targets.name: Indian Summer

targets.approach: Starting in Miter Basin, ascend the drainage below Iridescent Lake over gentle slabs and grassy meadows. At the outlet, skirt the east shore, get past a short third-class step, and take ledges up to the wall. Buns Of Steel breaches the headwall of the main tower.
targets.descent_text: Either rappel the neighbouring route Civilized or walk off.
targets.name: Buns Of Steel

targets.approach: Starting in Miter Basin, ascend the drainage below Iridescent Lake over gentle slabs and grassy meadows. At the outlet, skirt the east shore, get past a short third-class step, and take ledges up to the wall. Civilized starts at a V-shaped crack in the middle of the white tower.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route. All the anchors are two-bolt stations with links.
targets.name: Civilized

targets.approach: Starting in Miter Basin, ascend the drainage below Iridescent Lake over gentle slabs and grassy meadows. At the outlet, skirt the east shore, get past a short third-class step, and take ledges up to the wall. The route lies at the right of the white triangular pillar that makes up the wall's left portion. Two chimney features sit at the base; the first pitch starts up the side of the right-hand chimney.
targets.descent_text: To rappel the route, stop at the final bolted anchor, at the right edge of the pillar's top. The headwall above adds a short stretch to the true top.
targets.name: Iridescent Flow

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. This route is on Mega Dome, uphill and southeast of base camp, and takes the crack and ramp system left of the huge roof on the dome's north face.
targets.descent_text: After the last pitch, belay on the slabs above, walk the ridge east and rappel from slings on the north side of the dome.
targets.name: Bigger than Life

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The line follows the long, rounded arete just north of the formation that carries an obvious V-shaped feature, finishing in a crack system right of the arete.
targets.name: California Dreamin'

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. It starts on the northwest arete of the shark-fin dome that sits above and south of Mega Dome.
targets.name: Digitally Remastered

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The line takes the arete that has a prominent roof or arch partway up it.
targets.name: If 60's were 90's

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The route is on Sugar Pine Dome itself and climbs a left-facing chimney to a bolted belay.
targets.descent_text: Rappel south from the bolted belay.
targets.name: Sugar Pine Dome Unfinished Climb!

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The route climbs the knife-edge arete on the south face of Sugar Pine Dome, starting with a layback off the ground into a corner.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route with a single rope to the ground.
targets.name: The Edge of Sanity

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. It lies on the formation with the V-shaped feature, just south of California Dreamin', and takes the right-hand crack; belay below the roof and traverse left under it.
targets.name: 'V'

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The route is on the longest arete here, recognisable by a long right-facing dihedral low on the line; it is not quite the northernmost crag.
targets.name: Waiting to Exhale

targets.approach: From the Horseshoe Meadows trailhead, hike up to Long Lake, a good spot to camp. The buttress shows through and above the trees to the northeast. The route starts around the corner left of Magic Staircase, on a clean white face cut by a hand crack, right below that route's second-pitch corner.
targets.descent_text: The climbs on this buttress are gear-only and the descent is a walk-off.
targets.name: Devil's Snare

targets.approach: From the Horseshoe Meadows trailhead, hike up to Long Lake, a good spot to camp. The buttress shows through and above the trees to the northeast. Look for the prominent second-pitch corner about halfway up the face, to the left of the wall's highest section; the first pitch is blocky fourth class to easy fifth class up to its base.
targets.descent_text: Build a gear belay at the top of the second pitch and walk off.
targets.name: Magic Staircase

targets.approach: Neanderthal Wall is the pyramid-shaped granite wall seen to the northeast on the drive north into Kernville. It needs a rugged hike, either from Chimney Peak Road on the north or from Fay Ranch on the south. The route starts a good way left of Cro-Magnon Man, up a crack that lies just right of a left-facing corner, then traverses right to a vertical crack system, water groove and chimney to the top.
targets.name: Alley-Oop

targets.approach: Neanderthal Wall is the pyramid-shaped granite wall seen to the northeast on the drive north into Kernville. It needs a rugged hike, either from Chimney Peak Road on the north or from Fay Ranch on the south. The route follows the crack system that forms the longest continuous line from the foot of the pyramid to its summit.
targets.name: Cro-Magnon Man

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. Start at the base of the steep, right-leaning crack and corner system whose top is some way below a short, prominent offwidth.
targets.name: Grendel

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. Start at the thin crack running up the right edge of a tall flake, far beneath a vegetated offwidth.
targets.name: Marmot Fur Slippers
